title: Ultraproducts: truth modulo an ultrafilter

based_on.title: Model Theory for Algebra and Algebraic Geometry, Orsay sections 1–3

summary: Combine structures using an ultrafilter, prove Łoś's theorem, and obtain compactness for arbitrary set-sized languages.
abstract: A sequence of natural numbers may eventually exceed every fixed bound. Can we treat that sequence as one new number while keeping the first-order truths of the natural-number order? An ultrafilter tells us which sets of indices count as large. We identify sequences that agree on a large set and interpret relations by asking where they hold. Łoś's theorem shows that this rule works for every first-order formula, including quantified statements. The same construction combines different structures: if every finite part of a theory has a model, their ultraproduct supplies one model of the whole theory. This proves compactness even when the language has uncountably many symbols.
